mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary easing, which lowers discount rates and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy phase, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1300 thousand units, it signals a strengthening housing sector that boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1300, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 255, it indicates elevated inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 255, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) exceed 525,000 million dollars, it signals strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 525000, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
